evidence.text: The company is building what it calls an “agentic cloud”, infrastructure designed specifically for AI agents rather than adapted for them.

An encrypted-by-default network linking every node, with you holding the keys. Infrastructure Web Services 05 Agentic Runtime Your agents. Your boundary. Hundreds of independently operated nodes, live across dozens of countries, no central operator, no single view of the whole. Encryption: Unbreakable by design, not by promise. Every node is disposable and instantly replaceable, the network doesn't just resist failure, it's designed to shrug it off. Capacity: A global supercomputer, not a rented slice. Not promised in policy. Contact us FAQ: Questions, answered 01 What is Granite? Granite is full-stack AI infrastructure, architected from scratch for the agentic era, not adapted from legacy cloud. Two ways in: deploy and own your own dedicated infrastructure with Granite Infrastructure, or consume dedicated compute, storage and an agentic runtime across the network with Granite Web Services. Both run on the same foundation, so the guarantee of control is identical whichever you choose. 02 What does "full control" actually mean here? That your data, your encryption keys and your agentic runtime stay inside the boundary you choose, enforced by the architecture, not promised in a policy document. Nothing leaves that boundary unless you decide it does, and no outside entity can quietly compel access. 03 Can I start on Granite Web Services and deploy Granite Infrastructure later? Yes. It's one foundation, so you can consume capacity on Granite Web Services today and deploy your own unit when the time is right. Deployed Granite Infrastructure units interconnect to become part of the same network. 04 What do I need to host a Granite Infrastructure unit? A prepared pad, a power connection and cooling. The unit is a self-contained, liquid-cooled container that deploys at your chosen site in months rather than years. Final power, GPU and footprint specifications are confirmed against your site. 05 Which AI models can I run? Any of them. Granite Web Services is model-agnostic, bring open-weight or licensed models and swap them as the field moves. Because value sits in the runtime rather than the model, open-weight proliferation works in your favour. And you always keep the keys: not your key, not your agent. 06 Where does my data live, and can I get it out? Wherever you choose, and it stays there by architecture. There's no egress lock-in, so you're never penalised for moving data. 07 What runs underneath both products? A stateless operating layer shared by both products. It makes every node disposable and rebuildable, so control and resilience become properties of the system itself rather than of any single machine. 08 Does Granite help with regulatory compliance? Yes. Granite Web Services ships with a Compliance Pack, controls built into the platform rather than bolted on afterwards, designed to support obligations under major regulatory frameworks. It complements, rather than replaces, your own legal and compliance review. 09 Where are you today, and how do I start? The platform is live and in deployment today, with the first unit shipping in 2026. To begin, talk to us, reserve a node on Granite Web Services, or plan a deployment with Granite Infrastructure. zh.summary: 从能源旁的模块化数据中心到代理编排，提供强调自有控制的计算栈。
zh.judgment: 控制权主张有明确买方，但供电、建设和运营交付决定是否优于现有云。
zh.replaces: 团队分别谈机房与能源、采购硬件，再组合存储、网络、推理和代理运行环境。
zh.segment: 代理基础设施与自有计算
zh.product: 官网展示专用计算、GPU、存储、网络、代理运行与合规层，强调硬件适配和客户持钥。部署速度和安全效果属于公司主张，本次没有核验实地机房。
zh.customer: 对数据控制、地域与专用资源有要求的 AI 团队是潜在买方。它更接近基础设施采购，普通开发者的轻量原型未必需要全栈控制。
zh.workflow: 公司描述在能源附近布置模块化设施，再在统一栈中运行模型与代理。可验证交付涉及能源容量、设备安装、隔离、运行与维护，不能只验一层软件接口。
zh.business_model: 官网列出自购基础设施与通过网络消费服务两条路径，没有完整价格。前者承担资本与维护责任，后者需要核算使用、容量和服务承诺。
zh.traction: 本次支持的是产品栈与商业路径的公开描述，未取得独立部署周期或客户持续负载。所有权主张也需合同和实际管理权限确认。
zh.moat: 能源与硬件部署、系统编排和客户控制可能形成组合优势。大型云、机房服务商和自建都是替代；硬件无锁定能否落实需迁移测试。
zh.funding_read: 早期资金可支持栈验证，却无法证明建设周期或供电可得性。下一里程碑是可验收项目和持续负载，而不是扩大宣传的容量。
zh.risks: 能源许可和现场条件可能拖慢上线，硬件维护需要长期能力。客户持钥若没有清晰恢复机制，也可能把控制权变成额外运营负担。
zh.takeaway: 用完整责任链解释“可控基础设施”：谁持钥、谁维护、谁承担停机。把能源、资产和运行边界一起交付，而不是只销售自主标签。
zh.watch_next: 看真实建设周期、持续可用容量、客户负载与运维成本。分开比较资产购买和消费服务的合同、恢复责任及退出成本。

en.summary: A stack from modular energy-adjacent data centers to agent orchestration, emphasizing customer control.
en.judgment: Supply, construction and operating delivery determine whether control beats existing cloud alternatives.
en.replaces: Separately arranging energy, facilities, hardware, storage, networking, serving and agent runtime.
en.product: The site describes dedicated compute, GPUs, storage, networking, runtime and compliance layers, with hardware flexibility and customer-held keys. Speed and security claims were not field-verified.
en.customer: AI teams requiring data, geographic or dedicated-resource control are plausible buyers. This is infrastructure procurement; lightweight prototypes may not need the whole stack.
en.workflow: The described path places modular facilities near energy, then runs models and agents on a common stack. Energy, installation, isolation, operations and maintenance require joint acceptance.
en.business_model: The site offers owning infrastructure or consuming network services, without full public prices. Ownership brings capital and upkeep responsibilities; services require capacity and assurance cost comparisons.
en.traction: Public material establishes architecture and routes to market, not independent deployment times or sustained customer load. Contractual ownership and effective administrative control need confirmation.
en.moat: Energy access, installation and orchestration could create combined advantages. Clouds, colocation and self-build are substitutes; practical portability needs migration tests.
en.funding_read: Early capital supports stack validation without proving construction speed or power availability. Accepted projects and continuing workloads are better milestones than advertised capacity.
en.risks: Permitting and site conditions can delay delivery, and hardware needs long-term service. Customer-held keys without recovery plans can add operational burden.
en.takeaway: Explain control through responsibility: who owns keys, maintains systems and bears downtime. Deliver energy, asset and runtime boundaries together.
en.watch_next: Watch construction time, usable capacity, customer loads and operating cost. Compare ownership and consumption separately on contracts, recovery and exit cost.
